editorial:
You follow a group of college activists who fly from New York to the Amazon rainforest to protest logging. At first, it feels like a noble adventure with a cause. But once they land, things go wrong fast. The movie quickly turns from a feel-good mission into a nightmare survival story. The jungle looks beautiful but hides real danger. You watch these young idealists realize their good intentions mean nothing to the people living there. The tone shifts from hopeful to terrifying in minutes, and that sudden change keeps you on edge.

The standout here is the raw, old-school gore. If you like practical effects and intense survival scenes, this delivers. The acting is decent, though some characters feel like stereotypes. The pacing is relentless once the horror starts. On the downside, the movie leans hard into shock value and can feel mean-spirited. It is not for sensitive viewers. If you enjoy extreme horror and can handle graphic content, give it a shot. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the surviving activist escapes the cannibal village and makes it back to New York. She lies to the press, claiming the tribe is peaceful and needs protection. This twist reveals she is still using the tribe for her own cause. The last shot shows the tribe leader watching a video of her speech, hinting the danger is not over. You realize her activism was never about saving anyone but herself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves extreme survival horror and practical gore effects.
